boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented campus places for studying, making, viewing art, and taking a deliberate break between classes.

cards.title: Pause at Denny Chimes
cards.subtitle: The Quad
cards.notes: Use the Quad landmark as a meeting point, then listen for the carillon’s noon Alma Mater before heading to your next stop.
cards.short_summary: A working 25-bell carillon that marks time from the Quad.
cards.evidence_claim: UA identifies Denny Chimes as a 115-foot campanile on the Quad with a 25-bell carillon that plays the Alma Mater at noon.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor Quad landmark; check the university calendar for programmed events.

cards.title: Start at Gorgas Library
cards.subtitle: Main library on the Quad
cards.notes: Choose an individual or group study area, use library research support, and plan your work around the building’s posted hours.
cards.short_summary: UA’s main library for humanities, social sciences, and government information.
cards.evidence_claim: UA Libraries describes Gorgas as the campus’ main library and directs users to individual and group study spaces.
cards.access_notes: Library access and hours can change; consult the UA Libraries hours listing before visiting.

cards.title: Set up in the Learning Commons
cards.subtitle: First floor, Gorgas Library
cards.notes: Bring a project partner or work solo at the first-floor commons, where campus computers support academic software and library resources.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor workspace with computers and room for solo or group projects.
cards.evidence_claim: UA Libraries says the Gorgas Library Learning Commons provides computers with productivity and academic software and space for group or individual study.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Gorgas Library; follow current library access rules and posted hours.

cards.title: Make a media project at Sanford
cards.subtitle: Second floor, Gorgas Library
cards.notes: Reserve time or ask staff about available media-production support when a class project needs more than a laptop and headphones.
cards.short_summary: A digital-media production facility inside Gorgas Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UA Libraries identifies the Sanford Media Center on Gorgas Library’s second floor as a facility for digital media production for students.
cards.access_notes: Located inside Gorgas Library; confirm current Media Center hours and equipment policies before visiting.

cards.title: Walk the Woods Quad Sculpture Garden
cards.subtitle: Between Woods, Manly, Garland, and Clark Halls
cards.notes: Take the connecting sidewalks through the sculpture beds and use the benches for a short outdoor reset between nearby classes.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor gallery integrated into a historic academic quad.
cards.evidence_claim: UA says Woods Quad was developed as an outdoor sculpture garden with connecting sidewalks, sculpture beds, benches, and student and faculty work.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; use normal campus pedestrian routes and observe any temporary event or maintenance notices.

cards.title: See what is on view at Sarah Moody
cards.subtitle: 103 Garland Hall, Woods Quad
cards.notes: Check the current exhibition listing, then make time for a quiet visit to the contemporary-art gallery between classes on Woods Quad.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery with changing contemporary-art exhibitions and a permanent collection.
cards.evidence_claim: UA’s Department of Art & Art History says the Sarah Moody Gallery presents changing contemporary-art exhibitions and is located in Garland Hall.
cards.access_notes: A 2025 UA gallery notice lists weekday hours during the academic session; verify the current exhibition schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Browse Smith Hall’s natural-history museum
cards.subtitle: Smith Hall
cards.notes: Build in time to view the museum’s natural-history displays, then confirm its calendar because it closes for University holidays and home football games.
cards.short_summary: UA’s natural-history museum in Smith Hall.
cards.evidence_claim: UA Museums lists the Alabama Museum of Natural History in Smith Hall and publishes Monday–Saturday public hours, with holiday and home-game closures.
cards.source_title: Contact Us — The University of Alabama Museums
cards.access_notes: Published hours are Monday–Saturday, 9 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; closed on UA holidays and home football games.

cards.title: Step into Gorgas House Museum
cards.subtitle: 810 Capstone Drive
cards.notes: Plan a daytime visit to this historic campus house, and check the museum schedule before going because visits follow limited weekday hours.
cards.short_summary: A historic UA museum housed in the oldest surviving structure on campus.
cards.evidence_claim: UA identifies Gorgas House Museum at 810 Capstone Drive and lists weekday public hours with a midday closure.
cards.source_title: Contact Us — The University of Alabama Museums
cards.access_notes: Published hours are Monday–Friday, 9 a.m.–noon and 1–4:30 p.m.; closed on UA holidays.

cards.title: Take the trail at the UA Arboretum
cards.subtitle: 4801 Arboretum Way
cards.notes: Use the posted trail map for a daytime walk among the collections, and leave enough time to return before the daily sunset closing.
cards.short_summary: A university arboretum with a trail map, daily daylight access, and free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The UA Arboretum states that it is open daily from 8 a.m. to sunset and that admission is free.
cards.source_title: Visit Us — The University of Alabama Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Open daily 8 a.m.–sunset; closed New Year’s Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas.

cards.title: Record in a Gorgas Whisper Booth
cards.subtitle: First floor, Gorgas Library
cards.notes: Reserve a booth for a focused recording session when you need sound isolation, an iMac, microphone, and keyboard for a class project.
cards.short_summary: Reservable sound-isolation booths for individual media work.
cards.evidence_claim: UA Libraries says Gorgas Library’s first-floor Whisper Booths have iMacs, recording software, Yeti microphones, and 88-key keyboards and can be reserved.
cards.source_title: Equipment — The University of Alabama Libraries
cards.access_notes: Reservations are listed in four-hour periods up to two weeks ahead; confirm availability through the library booking link.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten no-purchase activities for enrolled UA students or the public, using documented complimentary membership or free admission.

cards.title: Walk the UA Arboretum trails
cards.subtitle: 4801 Arboretum Way
cards.notes: Bring a friend for a daylight trail walk, then use the printable trail map to choose a route through the woodland and gardens.
cards.short_summary: A free botanical preserve with trails, gardens, and outdoor spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Admission is free; the Arboretum is open daily from 8 a.m. to sunset.
cards.source_title: Visit Us – The University of Alabama Arboretum
cards.access_notes: Open daily, 8 a.m.–sunset; closed New Year's Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas.

cards.title: See work at Sella-Granata Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Woods Hall, 109 Seventh Avenue
cards.notes: Stop in during the academic term to view the current exhibition together; check the gallery’s posted schedule before making the walk.
cards.short_summary: A campus gallery where admission is free and open to the public.
cards.evidence_claim: The gallery is at 109 Woods Hall and admission is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: BFA Graphic Design Students Present Thesis Exhibition in Sella-Granata
cards.access_notes: The cited gallery notice lists term-time hours; confirm the current exhibition schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Browse the Transportation Museum
cards.subtitle: 1901 Jack Warner Parkway
cards.notes: Meet at Queen City Park and spend time with the transportation and local-history exhibits, then continue along the nearby riverfront.
cards.short_summary: A free public museum in Queen City Park by the Black Warrior River.
cards.evidence_claim: The Mildred Westervelt Warner Transportation Museum is free to the public.
cards.source_title: Swimming Together – The University of Alabama Museums
cards.access_notes: The cited museum page lists Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; verify before travel.

cards.title: Take a Hallowed Grounds campus tour
cards.subtitle: Meets at the Gorgas House Museum historic marker
cards.notes: Arrange or join this outdoor walking tour to examine UA’s slavery history with a graduate-student or faculty guide.
cards.short_summary: A free, public 45-minute walking tour based on archival research.
cards.evidence_claim: Hallowed Grounds tours are free and open to the public and last approximately 45 minutes.
cards.source_title: Hallowed Grounds Tours – Department of American Culture & Society
cards.access_notes: Group tours may be arranged pending docent availability; requests should be made at least two weeks ahead.

cards.title: Move together at the Student Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: University Recreation facility
cards.notes: Use your ACT Card with a fellow enrolled student for a workout, indoor track session, or court time without buying a membership.
cards.short_summary: A UREC facility included in complimentary enrolled-student membership.
cards.evidence_claim: UA student memberships are complimentary and include access to the Student Recreation Center.
cards.access_notes: For enrolled UA students registered for one credit hour or more; an ACT Card is required for entry.

cards.title: Plan a Witt Activity Center session
cards.subtitle: University Recreation facility
cards.notes: Coordinate a casual fitness or recreation session with another enrolled student and enter using the membership already loaded to your ACT Card.
cards.short_summary: A UREC activity center included with enrolled-student membership.
cards.evidence_claim: UA student memberships are complimentary and include access to the Robert E. Witt Activity Center.
cards.access_notes: For enrolled UA students registered for one credit hour or more; an ACT Card is required for entry.

cards.title: Swim at the UA Aquatic Center
cards.subtitle: University Recreation facility
cards.notes: Bring a qualifying enrolled-student friend for a swim session and review facility guidance before heading over with your ACT Card.
cards.short_summary: An aquatic facility covered by complimentary enrolled-student membership.
cards.evidence_claim: UA student memberships are complimentary and include access to the Aquatic Center.
cards.access_notes: For enrolled UA students registered for one credit hour or more; an ACT Card is required for entry.

cards.title: Use the Outdoor Pool Complex
cards.subtitle: Outside the Student Recreation Center
cards.notes: Make a warm-weather plan with an enrolled student friend; student membership includes this pool complex without a separate membership purchase.
cards.short_summary: A seasonal outdoor pool complex included with enrolled-student membership.
cards.evidence_claim: UA student memberships are complimentary and include access to the Outdoor Pool Complex.
cards.access_notes: For enrolled UA students registered for one credit hour or more; access is included in UREC membership.

cards.title: Rally at the Tennis Court Complex
cards.subtitle: University Recreation facility
cards.notes: Set up a low-key tennis meet with another enrolled student and use the courts through your complimentary UREC membership.
cards.short_summary: A tennis facility included with enrolled-student UREC access.
cards.evidence_claim: UA student memberships are complimentary and include access to the Tennis Court Complex.
cards.access_notes: For enrolled UA students registered for one credit hour or more; an ACT Card is required for entry.

cards.title: Join a UREC group exercise class
cards.subtitle: University Recreation facilities
cards.notes: Choose a class format with friends and attend through your enrolled-student UREC access; check the current class schedule before you go.
cards.short_summary: Group exercise classes offered at no additional cost through UREC membership.
cards.evidence_claim: University Recreation lists free group exercise classes, and student memberships are complimentary for all enrolled UA students.
cards.access_notes: For enrolled UA students registered for one credit hour or more; confirm the current class schedule and entry requirements.

cards.subtitle: Gorgas Library • Floor 1

cards.evidence_claim: UA Libraries lists group tables and soft seating throughout this loud study area.
cards.access_notes: Open seating; confirm current Gorgas Library hours before going.

cards.subtitle: Gorgas Library • Floor 2

cards.evidence_claim: UA Libraries lists group tables and seating throughout the quiet area, plus graduate and faculty carrels by reservation.

cards.entity_name: Gorgas Library Silent Study Area, Floor 4
cards.title: Gorgas Library Silent Study Area, Floor 4
cards.subtitle: Gorgas Library • Floor 4

cards.evidence_claim: UA Libraries identifies Floor 4 as a silent study area with group tables and seating throughout the floor.

cards.title: Gorgas Collaborative Space 1

cards.notes: Reserve this compact collaboration room for a project meeting that needs a shared screen or a connected Dell workstation.

cards.evidence_claim: UA Libraries lists Gorgas Collaborative Space 1 with a 55-inch 4K TV, Dell workstation, and laptop connection for up to five people.
cards.access_notes: Available by reservation; capacity is listed as up to five people.

cards.title: Gorgas Collaborative Space 2
cards.subtitle: Gorgas Library • Floor 2
cards.notes: Book this room when your group needs to connect a laptop to a shared 55-inch screen while keeping the team small.
cards.short_summary: A second reservable Gorgas collaboration room for small teams.
cards.evidence_claim: UA Libraries lists Gorgas Collaborative Space 2 with a 55-inch 4K TV, Dell workstation, and laptop connection for up to five people.
cards.access_notes: Available by reservation; capacity is listed as up to five people.

cards.title: Sanford Media Center
cards.subtitle: Gorgas Library • Floor 2
cards.notes: Use the media lab to edit a class video, design graphics, or work through an audio project with software and staff support.
cards.short_summary: A multimedia creation and instruction lab inside Gorgas.
cards.evidence_claim: UA Libraries describes the Sanford Media Center as a multimedia creation and instruction lab with Adobe Creative Suite, music-production, and video-editing software.
cards.access_notes: Only currently enrolled UA students may use the center; bring a valid UA Action Card. Computer stations may be reserved.

cards.entity_name: Angelo Bruno Business Library Study Spaces
cards.title: Angelo Bruno Business Library Study Spaces
cards.subtitle: Angelo Bruno Business Library • Culverhouse complex
cards.notes: Pick from the library’s seating options for solo work, then shift to a group study room or quiet talking area as needed.
cards.short_summary: Business-library seating, workstations, group rooms, and a quiet talking area.
cards.evidence_claim: The Bruno Library lists numerous study-space seating types, group study rooms, a quiet talking area, and workstations with high-demand software.
cards.access_notes: Located within the Culverhouse complex; check current library hours and room-reservation availability.

cards.title: Music Library Whisper Booths
cards.subtitle: Music Library • Gorgas Library, Floor 1
cards.notes: Reserve a booth to record voiceovers or simple keyboard and acoustic-instrument work; bring a USB drive for your files.
cards.short_summary: Two reservable recording booths with an iMac, microphone, and keyboard.
cards.evidence_claim: UA Libraries lists two Music Library whisper booths with a Yeti microphone, 88-key keyboard, and iMac with GarageBand.
cards.access_notes: Available by reservation to UA faculty, staff, and students; intended for recording rather than individual or group study.

cards.entity_name: Gorgas Library Graduate and Faculty Study Carrels
cards.title: Gorgas Library Graduate and Faculty Study Carrels
cards.subtitle: Gorgas Library • Floor 3

cards.access_notes: Faculty and graduate students only; one person per carrel, reservation required, and library closing time applies.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Alabama traditions spanning game day, campus milestones, and shared ceremonies.

cards.title: Elephant Stomp
cards.subtitle: Gorgas Library steps before home football kickoff
cards.notes: Arrive at Gorgas Library about an hour before kickoff to watch the Million Dollar Band and cheer squad’s pregame presentation.
cards.short_summary: A pregame gathering centered on the Million Dollar Band and UA cheerleading squad.
cards.evidence_claim: UA’s official gameday site says Elephant Stomp takes place at Gorgas Library one hour before kickoff; UA’s First Year Experience identifies it as the band and cheer squad’s pregame show.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled relative to kickoff; check the official gameday schedule for the specific game.

cards.title: Walk of Champions
cards.subtitle: North Endzone, Bryant-Denny Stadium
cards.notes: Plan to be outside the North Endzone 2.5 hours before kickoff to see this official gameday gathering and stadium approach.
cards.short_summary: A pregame stadium tradition tied to Bryant-Denny’s north endzone.
cards.evidence_claim: UA Gameday states that the Walk of Champions takes place outside Bryant-Denny Stadium’s North Endzone 2.5 hours before kickoff.
cards.access_notes: Timing is relative to kickoff; consult the official gameday schedule before traveling.

cards.title: Million Dollar Band
cards.subtitle: UA sporting events and football game days
cards.notes: Listen for the band during pregame and in the stadium; its music accompanies Alabama’s fight song and other cheering traditions.
cards.short_summary: UA’s more-than-century-old marching-band tradition is built into Crimson Tide game days.
cards.evidence_claim: UA First Year Experience says the Million Dollar Band has been a Crimson Tide tradition at sporting events and around campus for more than 100 years.
cards.access_notes: Performance details vary by event and game day.

cards.title: Sing “Yea, Alabama” After a Touchdown
cards.subtitle: Bryant-Denny Stadium game day
cards.notes: Join the fight song after an Alabama touchdown if attending a game; the Million Dollar Band provides the musical backing.
cards.short_summary: A stadium singalong that follows Alabama touchdowns.
cards.evidence_claim: UA First Year Experience calls singing the fight song after every Alabama touchdown a treasured Crimson Tide fan tradition.
cards.access_notes: Requires attendance at a football game; ticket requirements depend on the game.

cards.title: Hear the Noon Alma Mater at Denny Chimes
cards.subtitle: Denny Chimes, the Quad
cards.notes: Pause on the Quad around noon to hear the alma mater from Denny Chimes, then continue exploring the campus’s central green space.
cards.short_summary: Denny Chimes marks noon with UA’s alma mater.
cards.evidence_claim: UA states that Denny Chimes plays the alma mater daily at noon as a campus tradition.
cards.access_notes: The tower rings every quarter hour; the alma mater is identified by UA as a daily noon tradition.

cards.title: UA Ring Ceremony
cards.subtitle: Denny Chimes each spring
cards.notes: Eligible students can follow the spring ring-ceremony schedule: rings are placed inside Denny Chimes at 6:31 p.m. before formal presentation.
cards.short_summary: Class rings spend 24 hours inside Denny Chimes before the formal ceremony.
cards.evidence_claim: UA says official class rings are placed inside Denny Chimes at 6:31 p.m. each spring, then presented 24 hours later in a formal ceremony.
cards.access_notes: For official UA class rings; timing is scheduled each spring.

cards.title: Form the Script A
cards.subtitle: Weeks of Welcome at Saban Field, Bryant-Denny Stadium
cards.notes: New students can look for the Weeks of Welcome activity that forms a campus-wide Script A on Saban Field for a shared photo.
cards.short_summary: Freshmen assemble into the Script A during Weeks of Welcome.
cards.evidence_claim: UA documents that freshmen form the Script A on Saban Field during Weeks of Welcome, creating a photo with new friends.
cards.access_notes: Designed for freshmen during Weeks of Welcome; confirm current programming through UA orientation communications.

cards.title: Tapping on the Mound
cards.subtitle: Historic Mound on the west side of the Quad
cards.notes: Visit the Quad during Honors Day to observe honor societies tap new members on the Historic Mound, following posted ceremony guidance.
cards.short_summary: UA honor societies publicly tap new members during Honors Day.
cards.evidence_claim: UA News describes the Tapping on the Mound ceremony for four University honor groups as one of UA’s longest-standing traditions.
cards.source_title: April 2026 Events in Bloom at UA
cards.access_notes: The 2026 listing placed it at 1:30 p.m. on April 3; future dates should be confirmed with UA.

cards.title: UA Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Campus and downtown Tuscaloosa in the fall
cards.notes: Check the Homecoming schedule for the pep rally, parade, lawn decorations, and other official activities coordinated by the student board.
cards.short_summary: A fall return-to-campus celebration with parade, pep rally, and student-led competitions.
cards.evidence_claim: UA describes Homecoming as a fall tradition welcoming alumni with a pep rally, bonfire, downtown parade, and Homecoming Queen crowning.
cards.access_notes: Events, routes, and participation requirements are set annually by UA Homecoming.

cards.title: Recite the Capstone Creed
cards.subtitle: Key University of Alabama events
cards.notes: Learn the Creed before a major campus event; its text focuses on knowledge, fairness, integrity, respect, responsibility, and excellence.
cards.short_summary: A shared pledge recited at key UA events.
cards.evidence_claim: UA identifies the Capstone Creed as a tradition recited at key events and says it affirms commitments to honor, integrity, and respect.
cards.access_notes: Occurrence depends on the event; consult the relevant event program.

boards.title: Your First Weekend at The University of Alabama, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A walkable, under-21-safe sequence of campus landmarks, study space, food options, and cultural stops for getting oriented in Tuscaloosa.

cards.entity_name: Catherine and Pettus Randall Welcome Center
cards.title: Start at the Randall Welcome Center
cards.subtitle: 200 Bryce Lawn Dr. • Friday arrival
cards.notes: Begin with the visitor center’s galleries, films, photos, and artifacts, then use its campus context to choose the next stops on your walk.
cards.short_summary: An on-campus starting point for orientation and campus history.
cards.evidence_claim: UA identifies the Randall Welcome Center as an immersive visitor center with galleries, theaters, a lounge, and Alabama history and campus information.
cards.access_notes: The visitor guide says it is open to the public during normal UA business hours; confirm hours before visiting.

cards.title: Walk through the Quad
cards.subtitle: Central campus • Friday afternoon
cards.notes: Use the 22-acre green space as your bearings check: walk its paths, identify nearby historic buildings, and pause before heading to the chimes.
cards.short_summary: Campus’s central green space and gathering place.
cards.evidence_claim: UA describes the Quad as a 22-acre green space at the heart of campus and a central gathering place for celebrations and traditions.
cards.source_title: Profile of Excellence 2025–2026 | The University of Alabama
cards.access_notes: Outdoor space; use normal campus pedestrian access and follow posted event restrictions.

cards.title: Listen at Denny Chimes
cards.subtitle: The Quad • Friday afternoon
cards.notes: Stand at the 1929 tower on the Quad and listen for its timekeeping; schedule this stop near noon if you want to hear the alma mater.
cards.short_summary: A 25-bell carillon and defining campus landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: The official Denny Chimes site says the tower stands at the heart of the Quad, marks time, and plays the alma mater at noon.
cards.source_title: Denny Chimes | The University of Alabama
cards.access_notes: View from the Quad; the source documents a daily noon alma mater performance.

cards.title: Settle into Gorgas Library
cards.subtitle: The Quad • Friday afternoon
cards.notes: Take a study break in the Learning Commons, then note the Information Desk, media center, and group-study areas for future coursework.
cards.short_summary: UA’s main library for humanities, social sciences, and government information.
cards.evidence_claim: UA Libraries calls Gorgas the campus main library and lists study spaces, a Learning Commons, media center, and research assistance.
cards.source_title: Gorgas Library Description | The University of Alabama Libraries
cards.access_notes: Library hours can change during holidays, breaks, interim, and summer sessions; check before arrival.

cards.entity_name: The University of Alabama Student Center
cards.title: Get your bearings at the Student Center
cards.subtitle: Campus core • Friday evening
cards.notes: Use the Student Center to locate student-activity offices, meeting areas, the theatre, and food choices before deciding what to do next.
cards.short_summary: A campus hub for student activities, gathering spaces, and dining.
cards.evidence_claim: UA’s visitor guide says the Student Center contains a theatre, ballroom, conference rooms, student-government and student-activity offices, Starbucks, a food court, and the Supe Store.
cards.source_title: Campus Visitors Guide | The University of Alabama
cards.access_notes: Food vendors and building access may vary with the UA academic schedule.

cards.title: Read the Crimson Promenade pavers
cards.subtitle: Near the Student Center • Friday evening
cards.notes: Take the short walk beside the Student Center and look through the engraved pavers, which recognize UA students, alumni, leaders, and friends.
cards.short_summary: A brick walkway that records generations of UA connections.
cards.evidence_claim: UA states that Crimson Promenade, near the Student Center, celebrates students, alumni, leaders, and friends through personalized pavers.
cards.source_title: Paver Purchases | Division of Student Life
cards.access_notes: The walkway is near the Student Center; purchasing a personalized paver is optional and separate from viewing it.

cards.title: See natural history in Smith Hall
cards.subtitle: 427 Sixth Avenue • Saturday morning
cards.notes: Plan a daytime museum visit in Smith Hall to explore natural-history exhibits, and check the calendar because football home games and holidays affect hours.
cards.short_summary: UA museum stop with natural-history collections and exhibits.
cards.evidence_claim: The Alabama Museum of Natural History is in Smith Hall and lists regular Monday–Saturday hours of 9 a.m.–4:30 p.m., with stated exceptions.
cards.source_title: Hours, Location, Admission | Alabama Museum of Natural History
cards.access_notes: Regular hours are Monday–Saturday, 9 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; closed on UA staff holidays and football home games. UA students are listed as free.

cards.title: Take in the Walk of Champions
cards.subtitle: Outside Bryant-Denny Stadium • Saturday afternoon
cards.notes: Walk the exterior route at Bryant-Denny Stadium and look at its championship-team reliefs and coach statues; stay outside unless you have tour access.
cards.short_summary: An exterior campus landmark honoring Alabama football championships.
cards.evidence_claim: UA’s visitor guide says the Walk of Champions outside Bryant-Denny Stadium includes championship-team relief tributes and statues of championship-winning coaches.
cards.source_title: Campus Visitors Guide | The University of Alabama
cards.access_notes: The UA visitor guide identifies the exterior Walk of Champions as free and open to the public.

cards.title: Finish at Bryant-Denny Stadium
cards.subtitle: 920 Paul W. Bryant Dr. • Saturday afternoon
cards.notes: End the campus loop at the stadium exterior, then decide whether a separately scheduled tour fits your plans; do not assume field or interior access.
cards.short_summary: A major on-campus stadium and recognizable closing landmark.
cards.evidence_claim: UA’s visitor guide identifies Saban Field at Bryant-Denny Stadium as an on-campus facility and says stadium tours are sold online rather than available as walkups.
cards.source_title: Campus Visitors Guide 2025 | The University of Alabama
cards.access_notes: Exterior viewing is the conservative option. The guide says tours require online purchase and that walkups are not accepted.

cards.title: Close with the President’s Mansion
cards.subtitle: The Quad • Sunday morning
cards.notes: Circle back through the Quad to view this Greek Revival landmark from public outdoor areas and use it as a final reference point before leaving campus.
cards.short_summary: A historic UA landmark with nearly two centuries of campus presence.
cards.evidence_claim: UA describes the President’s Mansion as a Greek Revival home built in 1841 that survived the Civil War and has housed university presidents for nearly two centuries.
cards.source_title: Profile of Excellence 2025–2026 | The University of Alabama
cards.access_notes: View the exterior from public areas; no interior access is implied by the source.
